newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin says budget win keeps fiscal faith.
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin says budget win keeps fiscal faith.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik on Thursday praised parliament's approval of the 1997 draft budget in its first reading for protecting the country's fiscal reputation.
"I think responsible policy won," Kocarnik told reporters.

He said the four Social Democrats who crossed over to vote with the minority centre-right government late Wednesday were "responsible people who realised what failure to approve the budget would mean both internally...and externally".
Kocarnik said if the government's budget would have failed it would have meant "an increased cost of resources for the Czech Republic meaning (bond) ratings, etc."

The centre-right coalition has been in its toughest fight in five years over its fifth consecutive balanced budget plan, after falling two votes shy of a majority in parliament in June elections becuase of a strong showing by the Social Democrats.
Wednesday's vote locks in the budget totals with planned equal revenue and expenditure of 549.1 billion crowns, although details can be modified.
The whole package can still be killed in the final two readings, expected by mid-December.

Kocarnik said the "important thing" in Wednesday's vote was that "it is not possible to change the basic figures of the budget which were approved". He said now any increase in budget spending will have to be compensated by cuts elsewhere.
He rejected comments by some coalition partners who criticised the budget as leaning too far toward the Social Democrats positions on taxation and spending.
"I would not say the budget is Socially-democrtatic," Kocarnik said. "It is a certain compromise. It was necessary in order to have it approved unanimously by the coalition cabinet."
